answer: That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Because the velvet cliff is fixed at deposit and recorded in the horizon ledger, the copper audit publishes how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 15 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. That is 25 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
